question: Bind DEF, 5v5, anti-eco: ATK on eco (pistols/SMG). You hold A as Cypher (full-buy). How do you defend to minimize risk and maximize anti-eco win rate?

options.label: Play long-range angles, stay grouped with your A teammate, passively hold outside close-range SMG/pistol range
options.explication_courte: In an anti-eco you win long-range duels where pistols and shotguns are weakest; staying grouped avoids a surprise rush and preserves your rifles for the trades.

options.label: Set Trapwire + Spycam on the chokes and hold in retract for info + trades, without pushing for frags
options.explication_courte: Setup util plus passive info play is solid and safe, but slightly passive: you may cede space and let the eco rush closer than needed.

sources_option.citation: Hold passive map control and keep duels at long range; setting traps and info tools lets you play safe and trade rather than dueling up close.

options.label: Push aggresively into A Short to pick off the eco players before they set up
options.explication_courte: Chasing eco frags brings you into SMG/shotgun range where the eco is most dangerous: a grouped rush can punish your aggression and steal a rifle.

sources_option.citation: Don't chase eco frags into close-range positions; classic pistols and shotguns can win the day when numbers close the distance.

options.label: Solo-push into ATK spawn to take info early and fish for an isolated pick
options.explication_courte: Solo-pushing into ATK spawn on anti-eco means giving your rifle to a 5-stack eco group: you get swarmed and the round turns.

sources_option.citation: Against an eco, refrain from pushing into positions where the enemy can easily retrieve your weapon; stay on your own side of the map.

explication_longue:
Situation: Bind DEF, 5v5, anti-eco. ATK on eco (pistols, maybe SMG/shotgun). You hold A as Cypher with Trapwire, Spycam, Cyber-Cage (full-buy). Goal: win the round without giving up rifles.

Anti-eco principle: you cannot lose this round by playing standard, but you can lose it by playing wrong. The biggest mistake on anti-eco is chasing easy frags - it brings your rifles into close range where pistols and shotguns become viable. The correct line is passive and long-range: hold angles where your rifle dominates, stay grouped to deter the rush, and use Trapwire + Spycam for early warning.

Setup + passive hold (acceptable) is slightly more passive but still solid. Aggressive push into A Short (costly) is the classic anti-eco mistake: you step into shotgun range and gift the ATK a free rifle pick. Solo-pushing spawn (mistake) is a 1v5 on eco terms - you lose the rifle and the round.

Estimated elite distribution: ~54% passive long-range hold grouped, ~23% setup util + retract, ~17% aggressive push (costly), ~4% solo spawn push (mistake).

sources.citation: Sticking together, checking corners and keeping distance prevents surprise kills from pistols/shotguns; hold passive map control at long range.
Don't chase eco frags, refrain from pushing where the enemy can retrieve your weapons, and stay on your own side of the map.
In an anti-eco, minimize risk and maximize economy; keep players alive to preserve your buy and deny the enemy free weapon upgrades.
